critical_contracts: All 294 original requirements remain covered by 336 active requirements and 32 split lineages.
All 337 clause objects use the uniform exact_clause_text contract.
Top-level acceptance_test_ids and engineering_test_links equal the ordered clause test union.
Test IDs cover every introducing and revalidation gate and use active requirement IDs.
D-100 projection-authority amendment provenance is explicit.
D-102 reuse evidence names the exact pinned package rather than a stale version.
Lifecycle records show two blind rounds and the current v2.0.6 repair state.
M5a service requirement names exactly five services and excludes a backup agent.
The normative forbidden-surface vocabulary and term-sense exclusions are loaded directly by the validator.
Every forbidden domain and every permitted term sense is planted in the internal test suite.
Canonical JSON, clause register, decision register, lineage, split reasons, amendments and findings have workbook parity.
Forbidden-surface negation is sentence-local and token-bounded; unrelated substrings and cross-sentence negation cannot authorize a prohibited obligation.
Every term-sense allowlist ID and example ID exists in the active requirement set.
Forbidden-surface authorization is occurrence-linked: adversative clauses, double negation and exact sense phrases are enforced.
known_limits: Post-repair replay of disclosed mutations is diagnostic rather than fresh independent evidence.
Automated semantic rules do not replace Codex human review of product and architecture meaning.

The two blind mutation rounds challenged earlier validator versions. v1.0.4 is a focused post-Codex repair verified by new internal planted tests and the next independent Codex Package M0 review; no third blind round was scheduled under the agreed cap.
Novel semantic wording may require human review even when occurrence-linked scanning passes.
two_round_cap: No third blind round unless Codex identifies a P0 validator defect.
